title: Cyber Defenders Unit 1 · Messages on the move (6-8)

items.q: What does a checksum catch best?
choices: A changed packet whose count was fixed by an enemy
A packet damaged by accident, when its count no longer matches
A packet that took too many hops
A packet sent to the wrong address
items.why: A checksum is a count that travels with the packet. Damage changes the count, so the mismatch shows.

items.q: What three things can an interceptor do to an unsealed packet?
choices: Read it, seal it and speed it up
Copy it, number it and rebuild it
Read it, copy it and change it
Change it, hop it and check it
items.why: An unsealed packet is open to an interceptor: they can read it, copy it, and even change it.

items.q: A packet arrives with a word swapped, and its count still matches because the swapper fixed the count too. Which hole does this show?
choices: A changed message that a checksum alone cannot catch
A missing packet that was never resent
A busy router that needs another road
A copied packet kept by a stranger
items.why: The checksum matched because the swapper fixed it. That is the hole: a checksum alone cannot prove a message is untouched.

items.q: What does a padlock on a site certify?
choices: That the site is honest and safe
That everything it sells is good quality
That the trip is encrypted and the site controls its name
That no stranger can see the site's name
items.why: The padlock certifies the trip and the name: the connection is encrypted, and the site controls the name it shows.

items.q: A shop site shows a padlock, yet its prices are unreal and it pushes you to pay fast. How can it still be a trick?
choices: A scam site can have a sealed trip, because the padlock says nothing about honesty
A padlock makes every shop honest, so it cannot be a trick
The padlock proves the prices are real
Only unsealed sites can ever be tricks
items.why: A scam site can buy a padlock too. The padlock seals the trip; it never promises the shop is honest.

items.q: On a café network, a page opens unsealed and asks for private facts. What is the safest action?
choices: Enter the facts quickly, before anyone looks
Close the page and wait for a sealed connection you trust
Share only half of each fact
Ask a stranger at the next table to check it
items.why: Private facts on an unsealed page can be read by strangers on that network. Closing it and waiting is safest.

items.q: A photo is uploading from a tablet to online storage. Which state is the photo in?
choices: At rest, stored in the vault
In transit, moving between places
In use, open on the desk
At rest, because it will be stored later
items.why: Uploading means the photo is traveling between places: that is data in transit.

items.q: Which pairing fits the right lock to the right room?
choices: Van: lock the storage; vault: seal the trip
Van: seal the trip; vault: do nothing at all
Van: seal the trip; vault: lock it; desk: guard who sees it
Desk: seal the trip; vault: guard who sees it
items.why: Each state gets its own protection: seal data in transit, lock it at rest, and guard it in use.

items.q: Which pair names one benefit and one cost of the cloud vault?
choices: Easy backups and sharing; you trust another building's locks
No trust needed; nothing is ever copied
Faster hops; a longer address
Free storage forever; no locks are needed
items.why: The vault makes backups and sharing easy, and the cost is trust: another building's locks guard your things.
